units.text: Ahaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, ‘I am your slave and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising against me.’

Uriah the priest built the altar in accordance with everything King Ahaz sent from Damascus.
Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.

The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.
The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.
This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
The Lord will appear against them and destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth. All the islands of the nations will worship Him, each from his place.
You too, Ethiopians, are slain by My sword.

You will grow weak by day, and a prophet will also grow weak with you; I likened your mother to night.

My people were likened to one without knowledge. Because you thrust away recognition, I too will thrust you away from serving Me as priest. You forgot your God’s law, and I too will forget your children.
According to their multitude, so they sinned against Me; I will turn their glory into dishonor.
They will eat My people’s sins and take their souls amid their injustices.
It will be as with the people, so with the priest; I will exact punishment upon him for his ways and repay him for his schemes.
Woe to those going down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses and chariots because there are many, and in horses, a very great multitude, but not trusting Israel’s Holy One or seeking God!
He Himself, wise, brought evils upon them; His word will certainly not be set aside. He will rise against evil people’s houses and against their futile hope,
an Egyptian human being and not God, horses’ flesh, with no help. The Lord will bring His hand against them; the helpers will grow weary, and all will perish together.

For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”
For He abandoned His people, Israel’s house, because their country was filled, as from the beginning, with omens like the foreigners’ country, and many foreign children were born to them.
For their country was filled with silver and gold, and their treasures had no number; the land was filled with horses, and their chariots had no number.
The land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they bowed before what their fingers made.
A human being bowed down, and a man was humbled; I will certainly not let them go.
And now enter the rocks and hide in the earth from the Lord’s terror and the glory of His strength, whenever He rises to shatter the earth.
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and arrayed himself against Israel. He sent and called Balaam to curse you.
But the Lord your God was unwilling to destroy you. He blessed you abundantly, rescued you from their hands, and handed them over.

And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. And the inhabitants of Jericho fought against you, the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, Hittites, and Girgashites; and the Lord delivered them into your hands.
He sent the swarm of wasps before you, and it drove them out from before you, twelve kings of the Amorites, not by your sword or by your bow.
He gave you a land for which you did not labour, and cities which you did not build, and you were settled in them. You shall eat of vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant.
Now fear the Lord and serve Him with uprightness and righteousness. Remove the foreign gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods of your fathers beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But I and my house will serve the Lord, for He is holy.”

By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.
Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed, went away, returned, and lived in Nineveh.
As he was bowing down in the house of Neserach his god, his sons Adramelech and Sarasar struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Asordan became king in his place.
On that day there will be Jesse’s root and the one rising to rule nations; nations will hope in him, and his rest will be honor.
On that day the Lord will again show His hand, to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people left from the Assyrians, Egypt, Babylonia, Ethiopia, the Elamites, the sun’s rising and Arabia.
He will raise a signal to the nations and gather Israel’s lost ones; He will gather Judah’s scattered ones from the earth’s four wings.
Ephraim’s jealousy will be removed, and Judah’s enemies will perish. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not afflict Ephraim.

They will fly in foreigners’ ships toward the sea; together they will plunder those from the sun’s rising and Idumea. Upon Moab they will first lay their hands, and Ammon’s sons will be the first to obey.
and those remaining in Zion and left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all those recorded for life in Jerusalem,
because the Lord will wash away the filth of Zion’s sons and daughters and thoroughly cleanse the blood from their midst, by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.

He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
And they built Topheth’s altar, which is in the ravine of the son of Hinnom, to burn up their sons and daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in My heart.

Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.
And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.
From Thy sanctuary over Jerusalem, kings will bring Thee gifts.
Rebuke the beasts of the reed, the assembly of bulls among the heifers of peoples, so that those tested by silver may not be shut out; scatter nations that desire wars.
Envoys will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will hasten its hand toward God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; make music to the Lord. Diapsalma.
Make music to God, who rides upon the heaven of heaven toward the east; behold, He will give with His voice a voice of power.

Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising for testimony. My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to receive kings and pour all My furious wrath upon them; for all the earth will be consumed in My jealous fire.
For then I will change a tongue for peoples, for its generation, so that all call upon the Lord’s name and serve Him under one yoke.
From the far reaches of Ethiopia’s rivers they will bring sacrifices to Me.

On that day you will certainly not be ashamed of all the practices by which you acted impiously toward Me; then I will remove from you the contemptuous acts of your arrogance, and you will no longer boast upon My holy mountain.
I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will revere the Lord’s name,
Assemble and enter, all surrounding nations, and gather there! Let the meek become a fighter!
Let all the nations be roused and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Send out sickles, because the vintage is at hand! Enter and tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evils have multiplied.
Sounds rang out in the Valley of Judgment, because the Lord’s day is near in the Valley of Judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will sink their brightness.
And the earth was shaken and began to tremble; the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in His anger, and fire from His face set things ablaze; coals were kindled from Him.
And He bent heaven and came down, and gloom was beneath His feet.
And He mounted cherubim and flew; He flew on the wings of winds.
And He made darkness His hiding place; His tent was around Him, dark water in clouds of the air.
From the far-shining radiance before Him, the clouds passed— hail and coals of fire.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
You shall leave none of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it. Whatever remains until morning you shall burn with fire.
And this is how you shall eat it: your loins girded, your sandals upon your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to the Lord.
I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.
This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall celebrate it as a perpetual statute.
Lawlessness will burn like fire and be consumed by fire like dry grass; it will burn in the forest’s thickets and consume together everything around the hills.
Through the fury of the Lord’s anger the whole earth has been burned, and the people will be as though burned by fire. A person will not pity his brother,
but will turn to the right because he will hunger, and eat from the left; a person eating the flesh of his own arm will certainly not be filled.
For Manasseh will eat from Ephraim, and Ephraim from Manasseh, because together they will besiege Judah. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
He will say, “I will wait for God, who turned His face away from Jacob’s house, and I will put my trust in Him.”
Behold, I and the children God gave me—and it will be for signs and wonders in Israel’s house, from the Lord Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion.

If they say to you, “Seek those who speak from the earth and the belly-speakers, the empty-talkers who speak from the belly,” should not a nation turn to its God? Why do they seek the dead concerning the living?
For He gave law for help, so that they might speak unlike this utterance, concerning which there are no gifts to give for it.
A harsh famine will come upon you; when you hunger, you will be grieved and speak evil of the ruler and the cult images, and they will look up toward heaven above,
They will no longer be a hope for the house of Israel, bringing lawlessness to remembrance when they follow after them. They will know that I am the Lord.”
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first of the first month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his force to great servitude against Tyre; every head was bald and every shoulder was losing its hair. Yet neither he nor his force received wages for Tyre and the servitude they performed against her.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take her booty and strip her spoils; it will be wages for his force.
In exchange for his service, which he performed against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
On that day a horn will spring up for the whole house of Israel, and I will give you an opened mouth among them. They will know that I am the Lord.”
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the multitude of Egyptians by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,
him and his people: scourges from nations sent to destroy the land. They will all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land will be filled with wounded men.
I will make their rivers desolate and destroy the land and all that fills it by foreigners’ hands. I, the Lord, have spoken.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the magnates from Memphis and the rulers from the land of Egypt, and they will be no more.
I will destroy the land of Pathros, put fire upon Tanis, and execute vengeance in Diospolis,
Lament to Me more than a bride wrapped in sackcloth for her first husband.
Sacrifice and drink offering have been removed from the Lord’s house. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,
because the plains have suffered. Let the earth mourn, because grain has suffered, wine has dried up, and oil has diminished.
The farmers have dried up. Lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest from the field has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate, palm, apple tree and all the field’s trees have dried up, because human beings have put joy to shame.

Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.
Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,
As I returned, look—very many trees were on the river’s edge, on both sides.
He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.
Fishers will stand there from Aingadin to Ainagalim; there will be a drying place for nets. It will be by itself, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, an exceedingly great multitude.
At its outlet, at its turning, and at its overflow, they will certainly not be healed; they are given over to salt.

Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.
Cedar from Senir was built for you; strips of cypress planks were taken from Lebanon to make fir masts for you.
From Bashan they made your oars; they made your sacred places from ivory, wooded houses from the islands of Kittim.
Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt became your bedding, to clothe you with glory and wrap you in blue and purple from the islands of Elishah; it became your coverings.
Your rulers who inhabit Sidon, and the Arvadites, became your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, who were in you, were your pilots.
The elders of Byblos and their wise men were in you; they strengthened your counsel. All the ships of the sea and their rowers came to you toward the farthest west.
This book will be given into the hands of a person who does not know how to read. Someone will say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I do not know how to read.”
The Lord said, “This people draws near Me; with their lips they honor Me, but their heart is far from Me. They revere Me in vain, teaching human commands and teachings.
Therefore, behold, I will proceed to remove this people; I will remove them, destroy the wise people’s wisdom and hide the discerning people’s understanding.”

Woe to those making deep counsel, but not through the Lord! Woe to those making counsel in secret! Their deeds will be in darkness, and they will say, “Who has seen us, and who will know us or what we do?”
Will you not be reckoned as the potter’s clay? Will the formed thing say to its former, “You did not form me,” or the work to its maker, “You did not make me intelligently”?
Rejoice, heavens, because God had mercy on Israel! Sound trumpets, earth’s foundations! Cry out joy, mountains, hills and all their trees! For God redeemed Jacob, and Israel will be glorified.
Thus says the Lord who redeems you and forms you from the womb: “I am the Lord who completes all things. I stretched heaven alone and established the earth. Who else
will scatter the signs of spirit-mediums and divinations from the heart, turning the discerning backward and making their counsel foolish,

and establish His servant’s words and make His messengers’ counsel true? He says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be inhabited,’ and to Judea’s cities, ‘You will be rebuilt,’ and her deserted places will spring up;
He says to the abyss, ‘You will be desolate, and I will dry your rivers’;
him and his people: scourges from nations sent to destroy the land. They will all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land will be filled with wounded men.
I will make their rivers desolate and destroy the land and all that fills it by foreigners’ hands. I, the Lord, have spoken.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the magnates from Memphis and the rulers from the land of Egypt, and they will be no more.
I will destroy the land of Pathros, put fire upon Tanis, and execute vengeance in Diospolis,
and pour out My wrath upon Sais, Egypt’s strength, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.
I will put fire upon Egypt; Syene will be greatly troubled, and in Diospolis there will be a breach, and waters will pour out.
The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.
At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I shatter Egypt’s scepters there and the arrogance of her strength perishes there. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will be led away captive.
On that day the Lord Sabaoth will be the crown of hope, woven of glory, for My people who remain;
they will be left with a spirit of judgment, for judgment and strength, as He prevents destruction.
For these have been led astray by wine and wandered because of sikera. Priest and prophet lost their senses because of wine, reeled from sikera’s intoxication and went astray. This is an apparition.
A curse will consume this counsel, for this counsel is for greed.
To whom did we announce evils, and to whom did we announce a message—you weaned from milk, torn from a breast?
Expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little,
Syria from the sun’s rising and the Greeks from the sun’s setting, who devour Israel with their whole mouth. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
The people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
The Lord removed from Israel head and tail, great and small, in one day,
the elder and those who show favoritism—this is the leadership—and the prophet teaching lawless things—this is the tail.
Those blessing this people will lead astray, and they lead astray in order to swallow them up.

Therefore God will not rejoice over their young men, and He will not pity their orphans or widows, because all are lawless and evil, and every mouth speaks unjust things. For all these things the anger did not turn away, but the hand is still high.
Lawlessness will burn like fire and be consumed by fire like dry grass; it will burn in the forest’s thickets and consume together everything around the hills.
You too will become drunk and be overlooked; you too will seek a place to stand away from enemies.
All your fortresses are fig trees having lookouts; if shaken, they will fall into the eater’s mouth.
Look, your people within you are like women! The gates of your land will open wide to your enemies, and fire will consume your bars.
Draw water for yourself for the siege, hold your fortresses firmly; step into mud, be trampled in straw, hold fast over the brick.
There fire will consume you; a sword will destroy you, devouring you like a locust, and you will become heavy like a crawling locust.
Thou didst stretch forth Thy right hand; the earth swallowed them.
In Thy righteousness Thou didst guide this people of Thine whom Thou didst redeem; in Thy strength Thou didst comfort them to Thy holy dwelling.
The nations heard and were angry; pangs took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia.
Then the leaders of Edom hastened; and trembling seized the rulers of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
May fear and trembling fall upon them; by the greatness of Thine arm let them become as stone, until Thy people pass over, O Lord, until this people of Thine whom Thou hast purchased pass over.
Bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of Thine inheritance, in Thy prepared dwelling which Thou hast wrought, O Lord; the sanctuary, O Lord, which Thy hands have made ready.
The Lord reigns for ever and ever, and beyond.”
I said, “Only fear Me and accept discipline, and you will certainly not be destroyed from her eyes,” with all I exacted upon her. Prepare, rise early! All their gleaning has been ruined.

Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising for testimony. My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to receive kings and pour all My furious wrath upon them; for all the earth will be consumed in My jealous fire.
For then I will change a tongue for peoples, for its generation, so that all call upon the Lord’s name and serve Him under one yoke.
From the far reaches of Ethiopia’s rivers they will bring sacrifices to Me.

On that day you will certainly not be ashamed of all the practices by which you acted impiously toward Me; then I will remove from you the contemptuous acts of your arrogance, and you will no longer boast upon My holy mountain.
We did this out of concern about this matter, saying, ‘Tomorrow your children might say to our children, “What do you have to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
The Lord has made the Jordan a boundary between us and you, and you have no portion in the Lord.” Your sons would turn our sons away, so that they would not revere the Lord.’
We said that we should act in this way: build this altar, not for offerings and not for sacrifices,

but so that it may be a testimony between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform service to the Lord before Him with our offerings and our sacrifices and our sacrifices of well-being. Then your children shall not say to our children tomorrow, ‘You have no portion in the Lord.’

We said, ‘If ever they speak to us and to our generations tomorrow, they shall say, “Behold the likeness of the Lord’s altar which our fathers made, not for offerings or sacrifices, but as a testimony between you and us and between our sons.”’

May it never be that we turn away from the Lord in these present days, departing from the Lord by building an altar for offerings, salamin sacrifices, and a sacrifice of well-being apart from the Lord’s altar before His tent.”
When Phinehas the priest and all the leaders of the congregation of Israel with him heard the words spoken by the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were pleased.

And Phinehas the priest said to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, “Today we know that the Lord is with us, for you have committed no offence before the Lord, and you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord.”
The sons of Israel did evil before the Lord, forgot the Lord their God, and served the Baalim and the groves.
And the Lord was greatly angered against Israel, and sold them into the hands of Chousarsathom king of Syria of the Rivers; and they served him eight years.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord. The Lord raised up a saviour for Israel and saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother. And he heard him.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon him. He judged Israel and went out to war. The Lord gave Chousarsathom king of Syria into his hand, and his hand became strong against Chousarsathom.
The land was quiet for fifty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
The sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord. The Lord strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil before the Lord.
Judah will draw up for battle in Jerusalem and gather the strength of all the surrounding peoples: gold, silver and clothing in very great abundance.
This will also be the downfall of horses, mules, camels, donkeys and every animal in those camps, according to this downfall.
Whoever remains from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up each year to bow before the King, the Lord Almighty, and celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
Whoever among all the earth’s tribes does not go up to Jerusalem to bow before the King, the Lord Almighty—these will be added to those.
If Egypt’s tribe does not go up or come there, upon these too will be the downfall with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
This will be Egypt’s sin and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Tent-Pitching.
On that day what is upon the horse’s bridle will be holy to the Lord Almighty, and the cauldrons in the Lord’s house will be like bowls before the altar.

Every cauldron in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the Lord Almighty. All who sacrifice will come, take some of them and boil in them. No Canaanite will remain in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day.
“Let us go and return to the Lord our God, because He has seized us and will heal us; He will strike and dress our wounds.
He will restore us to health after two days; on the third day we will rise and live before Him.
We will know; we will pursue knowledge of the Lord. We will find Him ready like dawn, and He will come to us like rain, early and late upon the land.”
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away.
Therefore I mowed down your prophets; I killed them with the words of My mouth, and My judgment will go forth like light.

They will fly in foreigners’ ships toward the sea; together they will plunder those from the sun’s rising and Idumea. Upon Moab they will first lay their hands, and Ammon’s sons will be the first to obey.
The Lord will lay Egypt’s sea waste and bring His hand upon the river with a violent wind. He will strike seven ravines so that one may pass through it in sandals.
There will be a passage for My remaining people in Egypt, and it will be for Israel as on the day it came out of Egypt’s land.
And the Lord said to Abram, “Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, to the land that I will show you.
And I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be blessed.
And I will bless those who bless you, and those who curse you I will curse; and in you all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed.”
And Abram went as the Lord had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. Now Abram was seventy-five years old when he went out from Harran.

And Abram took Sara his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions they had acquired, and every soul they had acquired in Harran; and they set out for the land of Canaan, and came into the land of Canaan.
But what if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and to make His power known, endured with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
and did so to make known the wealth of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,
even us whom He also called, not only from Jews but also from Gentiles?
As He also says in Hosea, “I will call those who are not My people ‘My people,’ and her who is not beloved ‘beloved’;
and in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.”
But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “Though the number of Israel’s sons be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;
for the Lord will carry out a word on the earth, completing it and cutting it short.”
“And you, son of man, take a brick, set it before your face, and draw upon it a city—Jerusalem;
lay siege to it, build forward defenses against it, throw up a palisade against it, set camps against it, and arrange missile positions all around.
Take an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Prepare your face against it; it will be besieged, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.
Lie on your left side and place the injustices of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of days—one hundred fifty—that you lie upon it; bear their injustices.
I have assigned you their two injustices as a number of days, one hundred ninety days; bear the injustices of the house of Israel
You will do as I have done: you will not be comforted from their mouth or eat the bread of men,
with your hair upon your heads and your footwear on your feet. You certainly will neither beat your breasts nor weep; you will waste away in your injustices and each will comfort his brother.
Ezekiel will be a portent for you; according to everything he has done, you will do when these things come. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take their strength from them, the exaltation of their boasting, the desires of their eyes, the exaltation of their soul, their sons and daughters—
on that day the survivor will come to you to announce it into your ears?
“Come down and sit on the ground, virgin daughter Babylon. Enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called tender and pampered.
Take a millstone and grind flour. Uncover your veil, expose your gray hair, pull up your garments to bare your lower legs, and cross rivers.
Your shame will be uncovered, and your reproaches will be visible. I will exact justice from you; I will certainly no longer hand it over to humans.”
The One who rescued you said—His name is the Lord Sabaoth, Israel’s Holy One—
“Sit stricken and enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. You will certainly no longer be called a kingdom’s strength.
“Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,
you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.
For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain
toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”

The vision of the four-footed creatures in the wilderness. In affliction and hardship, a lion and lion cub from there, asps and offspring of flying asps; they carried their wealth on donkeys and camels to a nation that will not benefit them with help, but with shame and reproach.
Egyptians will benefit you with futile and empty things. Announce to them, “This consolation of yours is futile.”
At that time they will say to this people and Jerusalem: A spirit of wandering in the wilderness; the daughter of My people’s way is not toward purity or holiness.
A spirit of filling will come to Me; but now I speak judgments against them.
Behold, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a storm; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, because we suffer misery!
Wash your heart clean of evil, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will the schemes of your troubles exist within you?
For the voice of one announcing will come from Dan, and trouble will be heard from Mount Ephraim.
Wail, for the Lord’s day is near, and shattering will come from God.
Therefore every hand will slacken, and every human soul grow cowardly;
the envoys will be troubled, and labor pains will hold them like those of a woman giving birth. They will lament to one another and be distraught, and change their face as to flame.
For behold, the Lord’s incurable day comes, of wrath and anger, to make the whole inhabited world deserted and destroy its sinners from it.
For heaven’s stars, Orion and all heaven’s array will not give light; it will grow dark as the sun rises, and the moon will not give its light.
Like those guarding a field they came against her all around, because you neglected Me, says the Lord.
Your ways and your practices have done these things to you. This is your evil: it is bitter; it has reached to your heart.
My belly, my belly, I am in pain, and the senses of my heart! My soul rages, my heart is torn; I will not be silent, because my soul heard the sound of a trumpet, a cry of war.
It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.
How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?
For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.
I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.

King Baltasar held a great reception on the day of the dedication of his royal buildings and invited two thousand men from among his magnates. On that day Baltasar, elated by wine and boasting, praised all the nations’ cast and carved gods in his place, but gave no praise to God Most High. That very night fingers like a human’s came out and inscribed on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the lamp, “Mane, Phares, Thekel.” Their interpretation is: Mane, “It has been numbered”; Phares, “It has been taken away”; Thekel, “It has been weighed.”
King Baltasar held a great banquet for his companions and drank wine.

His heart was exalted, and he ordered the gold and silver vessels of God’s house that his father Nebuchadnezzar had brought from Jerusalem to be brought in, and wine poured in them for his companions.
They were brought, and they drank from them,
and blessed their handmade idols. But they did not bless the everlasting God, who had authority over their breath.
At that very hour fingers like those of a human hand came out and wrote on the plaster of his house’s wall, opposite the light and before King Baltasar. He saw a hand writing.
His appearance changed, and fears and apprehensions pressed upon him. The king hurried and rose to look at that writing, while his companions around him were boasting.
I will stand at my watch and step onto a rock; I will look out to see what He will speak within me and what I shall answer concerning my reproof.
The Lord answered me: “Write a vision clearly on a boxwood tablet, so that the one reading these things may pursue them.
For the vision is still for a season, and it will rise toward the end and not toward emptiness. If he delays, wait for him, for coming he will come and certainly will not linger.
If he draws back, My soul has no pleasure in him; but the righteous one shall live by My faithfulness.

But the wine-soaked, contemptuous, boastful man will accomplish nothing. He widened his appetite like Hades and is like death, never filled; he will gather all nations and receive all peoples to himself.
Wounded men will fall in the Chaldeans’ land, and pierced men outside her.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, of the Lord Almighty, because their land was filled with injustice from Israel’s holy ones.
Flee from Babylon’s midst; each of you save your life. Do not be cast away in her injustice, for her time of vengeance is from the Lord; He is repaying her recompense.
Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. Nations drank her wine; therefore they were shaken.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered. Lament her! Take resin for her corruption, if somehow she may be healed.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
