Now “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.
Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be grateful, and through this gratitude serve God acceptably with reverence and awe,
for indeed our God is a consuming fire.
When he burned Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria Zobah, and Joab returned and struck the Valley of Salt—twelve thousand.
God, Thou didst reject us and pull us down; Thou wast angry and hadst compassion on us.
Thou didst shake the earth and trouble it; heal its fractures, for it was shaken.
Thou didst show Thy people hard things; Thou madest us drink wine of stupor.
Thou gavest those who fear Thee a sign to flee from the face of a bow. Diapsalma.
For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their wounded and dead will be thrown out; their odor will rise, and mountains will be soaked with their blood.
Heaven will roll up like a scroll, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine, like leaves falling from a fig tree.
My sword became drunk in heaven. Behold, it will descend upon Idumea and upon the people of destruction, with judgment.
The Lord’s sword was filled with blood, thickened with lambs’ fat and the fat of male goats and rams, for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosor and a great slaughter in Idumea.
And many will follow their debaucheries, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
And in greed they will exploit you with fabricated words. Their judgment has not been idle since long ago, and their destruction does not sleep.
For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of gloom, kept for judgment,
and did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a herald of righteousness, as one of eight, when He brought a flood upon a world of ungodly people,
and reduced the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemning them to overthrow, having made them an example for those who would live ungodly lives,
For all the peoples will walk, each his own way, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and beyond.
“On that day,” says the Lord, “I will gather the crushed one, receive the expelled one and those I rejected.
I will make the crushed one a remnant and the rejected one a strong nation. The Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever.
And you, squalid tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, to you it will come and enter—the former rule, a kingdom from Babylon for the daughter of Jerusalem.”
And now why have you experienced calamities? Did you have no king? Has your counsel perished, that birth pains have seized you like a woman giving birth?
A psalm of David. Sing to the Lord a new song, for the Lord has done wonders. His right hand and His holy arm won salvation for Him.
The Lord made His salvation known; before the nations He revealed His righteousness.
He remembered His mercy to Jacob and His truth to the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth saw the salvation of our God.
Remember these things and groan. Repent, you who have wandered astray; turn back in heart.
Remember the former things from eternity, for I am God, and there is none besides Me,
announcing the last things beforehand, before they came to be—and together they were fulfilled. I said, ‘All My counsel will stand, and I will do everything I have planned,’
calling a bird from the east and from a distant land concerning what I have planned. I spoke and brought it about; I created and acted. I brought him and made his journey prosper.
Listen to Me, you who have lost heart, who are far from righteousness.
Behold, I am rousing the Medes against you, who do not value silver or have need of gold.
They will shatter young men’s arrows and certainly not pity your children; their eyes will not spare the children.
Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah.
She will not be inhabited for everlasting time, nor will people ever enter her through many generations. Arabs will certainly not pass through her, and shepherds will certainly not rest in her.
Wild beasts will rest there, and the houses fill with sound; sirens will rest there, and demons dance there.
Donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and hedgehogs make nests in their houses. It comes quickly and will not delay.
I will praise God’s name with a song and magnify Him in praise,
and it will please God more than a young calf bringing forth horns and hoofs.
Let the poor see and rejoice; seek God, and your soul will live,
for the Lord heard the needy and did not despise His bound ones.
Let the heavens and earth praise Him, the sea and everything creeping in them.
For God will save Zion, and Judea’s cities will be built; they will dwell there and inherit it.
And the Lord remains for ever; He prepared His throne for judgment,
and He will judge the inhabited world in righteousness; He will judge peoples with uprightness.
And the Lord became a refuge for the needy, a helper at fitting times in distress.
Let those who know Thy name hope in Thee, for Thou hast not abandoned those who seek Thee, Lord.
Sing praise to the Lord, who dwells in Zion; announce His deeds among the nations,
He gathered them from the countries, from east and west and north and the sea.
They wandered in the wilderness, in a waterless place; they did not find a road to a city of habitation,
hungry and thirsty; their soul failed within them.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He rescued them from their distresses,
and guided them into a straight way to travel to a city of habitation.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
for He filled an empty soul and filled a hungry soul with good things.
Those sitting in darkness and death’s shadow, fettered in poverty and iron,
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following, “Truly I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.
I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,
but the sons of the kingdom will be cast into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; as you have believed, let it happen for you.” And his servant was healed at that hour.
The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!
For He abandoned His people, Israel’s house, because their country was filled, as from the beginning, with omens like the foreigners’ country, and many foreign children were born to them.
For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.

There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the written saying will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
“Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
The stone the builders rejected— this has become the head of the corner.
This has come from the Lord, and is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day the Lord has made; let us exult and be glad in it.
O Lord, save now! O Lord, prosper us now!
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.
The Lord is God, and He has shone upon us. Arrange a festival among the thickly covering boughs, up to the horns of the altar.
Thou art my God, and I will thank Thee; Thou art my God, and I will exalt Thee. I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me and becamest my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy is for ever.
Now many nations have gathered against you, saying, “We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Zion!”
But they did not know the Lord’s thought or understand His counsel, for He gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.

Rise and thresh them, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze. With them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine; you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
Now the daughter of Ephraim will be fenced in with a barrier; he has set a constraint upon us. With a rod they will strike Israel’s tribes on the cheek.
Moab’s fugitives will sojourn with you; they will be a shelter for you from the pursuer, because your alliance was removed, and the ruler trampling the earth perished.
A throne will be set right with mercy, and one will sit upon it with truth in David’s tent, judging, seeking judgment and hastening righteousness.
We heard Moab’s insolence—exceedingly insolent. You raised up your arrogance. Your divination is not so,
not so. Moab will wail, for all in Moab’s country will wail. You will ponder for Deseth’s residents and not be ashamed.

Hesebon’s plains will mourn, and Sebama’s vine. You who devour the nations, trample her vineyards as far as Iazer; you will certainly not reach them. Wander in the wilderness! Those sent out were abandoned, for they crossed the wilderness.
Therefore I will weep like Iazer’s weeping for Sebama’s vine. He felled your trees, Hesebon and Eleale, because I will trample upon your grain harvest and vintage, and all will fall.
Akkarioth was taken and the fortifications seized.
Moab will perish from being a multitude, for he magnified himself against the Lord.
Trap, fear, and pit are upon you, resident Moab.
One who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and one who climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap, for I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.
two by two they entered the ark with Noah, male and female, as God had commanded him.
And after seven days the waters of the flood came upon the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the deep burst open, and the floodgates of heaven were opened.
And rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah entered the ark, with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with him.
Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but impiety falls into injustice.
The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but lawless people are caught in their own destruction.
When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the impious perishes.
The righteous escapes from the hunt, but the impious is handed over in his place.
In the mouth of the impious is a trap for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous has a good course.
You will suck the nations’ milk and eat kings’ wealth. You will know that I am the Lord who saves and delivers you, Israel’s God.
Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, instead of iron silver, instead of wood bronze, and instead of stones iron. I will appoint your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
Injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Engraving.
The sun will not be your light by day, nor will the rising moon light your night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light and God your glory.
For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail. The Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be fulfilled.
I will not die, but live, and tell in full the works of the Lord.
The Lord disciplined me with discipline, and did not hand me over to death.
Open for me the gates of righteousness; entering through them, I will give thanks to the Lord.
This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous will enter through it.
I will thank Thee, for Thou heardest me and becamest my salvation.
The stone the builders rejected— this has become the head of the corner.
Rejoice in the Lord always. Again I will say: rejoice.
Let your gentleness be known to all people. The Lord is near.
Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever are honorable, whatever are just, whatever are pure, whatever are lovely, whatever are well spoken of, if there is any excellence and if there is any praise, consider these things.
Practice the things you learned and received and heard and saw in me; and the God of peace will be with you.

For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.
But for you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; you will go out and leap like little calves released from bonds.
You will trample the lawless, because they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day that I am making,” says the Lord Almighty.
“And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,
who will restore a father’s heart toward a son and a person’s heart toward his neighbor, lest I come and strike the land utterly.”
Remove a crooked mouth from yourself and thrust unjust lips far away from you.
Let your eyes look straight, and let your eyelids incline toward righteous things.
Make straight tracks for your feet and direct your ways rightly.
Do not turn to the right or the left; turn your foot away from an evil way.
For God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are perverted.
He Himself will make your tracks straight and advance your journeys in peace.
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all Canaan’s kingdoms.
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
Lord, Thy name is for ever; Lord, Thy memorial is from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge His people and be comforted concerning His slaves.
The nations’ idols are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth but will not speak; they have eyes but will not see.
I was prepared and was not troubled to keep Thy commandments.
Sinners’ cords entangled me, and I did not forget Thy law.
At midnight I would rise to give thanks unto Thee for Thy righteous judgments.
I am a companion of all who fear Thee and of those who keep Thy commandments.
The earth is full of Thy mercy, Lord; teach me Thine ordinances.
It calls out misery and crushing, because the whole land has suffered misery; suddenly the tent has suffered misery, and my tent coverings have been torn apart.
How long will I see people fleeing while hearing the sound of trumpets?
For the leaders of My people did not know Me; they are foolish sons and not discerning. They are wise at doing evil, but did not learn to do well.
I looked upon the earth, and behold, nothing; and into heaven, and its lights were not there.
I saw the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were being shaken.
not abandoning our own gathering together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.
For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains,
but a fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire about to consume the adversaries.
Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without compassion on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, regarded as common the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
The Lord bless you and keep you;
the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you;
the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.

He still continued to sin, and they made themselves a cast image from their silver according to the likeness of idols, works completed for them by craftsmen. They say, ‘Sacrifice human beings, for calves have run out!’
Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like morning dew passing away, like chaff blown from a threshing floor and like vapor from locusts.

But I am the Lord your God, who establishes heaven and creates earth, whose hands created all heaven’s host. I did not display them to you so that you should follow them. I brought you up from Egypt’s land; you shall know no god except Me, and there is none who saves apart from Me.
I shepherded you in the wilderness, in an uninhabited land,
according to their pastures. They were filled to fullness, and their hearts were lifted up; for this reason they forgot Me.
In all these things they sinned still and did not believe in His wonders,
and their days failed in futility, and their years with haste.
Whenever He killed them, they sought Him; and they returned and rose early toward God,
and remembered that God is their helper, and God Most High is their redeemer.
And they deceived Him with their mouth, and lied to Him with their tongue,
but their heart was not upright with Him, nor were they faithful in His covenant.

Jesus knew that they wanted to ask Him, and said to them, “Are you seeking an answer among yourselves about this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you do not behold Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me’?
Amen, amen, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will become joy.

When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
So you too now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
And on that day you will ask Me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: if you ask the Father anything, He will give it to you in My name.
Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
A sound of shouting from the city, a sound from the temple, the sound of the Lord repaying recompense to His opponents!
Before the woman in labor gave birth, before the pain of labor came, she escaped and bore a male.
Who heard such a thing, and who has seen anything like it? Did a land labor in one day, or was a nation born all at once? For Zion labored and bore her children.
‘But I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me,’ said the Lord. ‘Behold, did I not make the woman who gives birth and the barren woman?’ said God.
Rejoice, Jerusalem, and celebrate in her, all who love her! Rejoice with joy, all who mourn over her,
so that you may nurse and be filled from her comforting breast, so that, nursing fully, you may delight in the entrance of her glory.
For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He also gave the Son to have life in Himself.
And He gave Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
and come out: those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who practiced base things to a resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing from Myself. As I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
If I bear witness concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.

“At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.
Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.
Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.
But you, Daniel, cover the commands and seal the book until the time of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice.”
You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.”
Moses called the whole council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them, “Go and take a sheep for your families, and slaughter the Passover.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood beside the door, and touch the lintel and both doorposts with the blood beside the door. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until morning.

The Lord will pass through to strike the Egyptians. He will see the blood on the lintel and both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the doorway. He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
And you shall keep this word as a statute for yourself and for your sons for ever.
And when you enter into the land which the Lord shall give to you, as He has spoken, you shall keep this service.
And Cain said to Abel his brother, “Let us go out into the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose against Abel his brother and slew him.
And God said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
And God said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries unto Me from the earth.
And now you are cursed from the earth, which opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
When you till the earth, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth.”
My belly is burned up from weeping, and a shadow lies upon my eyelids.
Yet there was nothing unjust in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh, and let there be no place for my cry!
Even now, behold, my witness is in the heavens, and the one who knows with me is in the highest places.
May my supplication reach the Lord, and may my eye drip tears before Him.
Why dost Thou turn away Thy hand and Thy right hand from within Thy bosom to the end?
But God is our King before the age; He worked salvation in the midst of the earth.
Thou didst strengthen the sea by Thy power; Thou didst crush the dragons’ heads upon the water.
Thou didst crush the dragon’s heads; Thou gavest him as food to the Ethiopian peoples.
Thou didst break open springs and torrents; Thou didst dry up rivers of Etham.
Thine is the day, and Thine is the night; Thou didst fashion light and the sun.
The pillars of heaven were spread out and were astonished at His rebuke.
By strength He calmed the sea, and by knowledge He wounded the great sea creature.
The bars of heaven have feared Him, and by a command He killed the rebellious dragon.
Behold, these are parts of His way, and we will hear a mere drop of speech concerning Him. But the strength of His thunder—who knows when He will act?”
I will sing now to the beloved a song of the loved one for my vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a horn, in a fertile place.
I put a fence around it, surrounded it with a palisade, planted a Sorech vine, built a tower in its midst and dug a wine vat in it. I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now, man of Judah and residents of Jerusalem, judge My case and the matter of My vineyard.
What more shall I do for My vineyard that I did not do for it? For I waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced thorns.
Now I will announce to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will remove its fence, and it will be plundered; I will pull down its wall, and it will be trampled,
and I will abandon My vineyard. It will certainly not be pruned or dug, and thorns will rise in it as in fallow ground. I will command the clouds not to rain upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.
Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?
For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: “If many houses come to be, great and beautiful, they will become deserted, and no one will inhabit them.
‘I will not take vengeance on you for ever or always be angry with you. For spirit will go out from Me, and I made every breath.
Because of sin I grieved him a little, struck him, and turned My face away from him. He was grieved and went gloomily along his ways.
I have seen his ways, healed him, comforted him, and given him true comfort—
peace upon peace to those far away and those near. And the Lord said, ‘I will heal them.’
But the unjust will be tossed by waves in this way and will be unable to rest.
‘There is no rejoicing for the ungodly,’ said the Lord God.”
Assur will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse, and we will certainly no longer call the works of our hands “Our gods.” The One in you will have mercy on an orphan.
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and settle beneath his shelter; they will live and be filled to intoxication with grain. His memorial will blossom like a vine, like Lebanon’s wine.
As for Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a thickly shading juniper; from Me your fruit is found.
Who is wise and will understand these things, or discerning and will recognize them? For the Lord’s ways are straight; the righteous will walk in them, but the impious will grow weak in them.
For if you were cut from what is by nature a wild olive, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that a partial hardening has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles enters,
and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
With regard to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with regard to election, beloved for the fathers’ sake.
For God’s gifts and calling are irrevocable.

The king pulled down the altars on the roof of Ahaz’s upper chamber which Judah’s kings had made, and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the Lord’s house. He tore them down from there and threw their dust into the Kidron torrent.

The king defiled the house facing Jerusalem, to the right of Mount Mosoath, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Astarte, the Sidonians’ offensive thing, for Chamos, Moab’s offensive thing, and for Molchol, the Ammonites’ abomination.
He shattered the pillars, destroyed the groves, and filled their sites with human bones.

Moreover, he tore down the altar at Bethel, the high place Jeroboam son of Nabat had made, who caused Israel to sin—both that altar and the high place. He shattered its stones, reduced it to dust, and burned the grove.

Josiah turned aside and saw the tombs there in the city. He sent and took the bones from the tombs, burned them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the Lord’s word which the man of God spoke while Jeroboam stood at the festival beside the altar. Turning, he lifted his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.
He said, ‘What is that rocky marker I see?’ The city’s men told him, ‘It is the man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words which he proclaimed against Bethel’s altar.’
The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem during the reign of Oziah, Joatham, Achaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
Listen, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord has spoken: “I begot sons and raised them high, but they rejected Me.
An ox knew the one who acquired it, and a donkey its lord’s manger; but Israel did not know Me, and the people did not understand Me.”
Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil offspring, lawless sons! You abandoned the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
Why should you be struck again as you add lawlessness? Every head is in pain, and every heart in grief.
From feet to head: for neither a wound nor a bruise nor an inflamed blow is there a poultice to apply, nor oil nor bandages.

And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before your face, and you receive them into your heart among all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you,
and you return unto the Lord your God, and obey His voice according to all that I command you this day, with all your heart and with all your soul,
then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
And the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.
Immediately after the affliction of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its brightness, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn; they will see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send His angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather His chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.

Isaiah 17:1.text: The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,

Isaiah 17:2.text: abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

Isaiah 17:3.text: There will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, nor a kingdom in Damascus, and the Syrians’ remainder will perish; for you are no better than Israel’s sons and their glory. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.

Isaiah 17:4.text: On that day Jacob’s glory will fail, and the fat parts of his glory will be shaken.

Isaiah 17:5.text: It will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps seed from the ears in his arm, as when someone gathers an ear in a firm ravine,

Isaiah 17:6.text: and a stalk is left in it, or like olive berries, two or three on a lofty top, or four or five left on their branches. Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God.

Isaiah 17:7.text: On that day a person will trust in the One who made him, and his eyes will look toward Israel’s Holy One,

Isaiah 17:8.text: and they will certainly not trust the altars or their hands’ works, which their fingers made, nor look at their trees or abominations.

Isaiah 17:9.text: On that day your cities will be abandoned as the Amorites and Hivites abandoned theirs before Israel’s sons, and they will be deserted,

Isaiah 17:10.text: because you abandoned God your Savior and did not remember the Lord your Helper. Therefore you will plant a faithless planting and faithless seed;

Isaiah 17:11.text: on the day you plant, you will wander. In the morning, if you sow, it will blossom for harvest on whatever day you allot, and like a human father you will allot to your sons.

Isaiah 17:12.text: Woe, the multitude of many nations! Like a surging sea, so you will be troubled, and the back of many nations will roar like water.

Isaiah 17:13.text: Many nations are like abundant water, like much water violently rushing down. He will drive him away and pursue him far off, like chaff-dust when people winnow before wind, and like wheel-dust carried by a squall.

Isaiah 17:14.text: Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will be gone. This is the portion of those who plundered you, an inheritance for those who took possession of you.

Isaiah 18:1.text: Woe, wings of a land of ships, beyond Ethiopia’s rivers,

Isaiah 18:2.text: the one sending hostages by sea and papyrus letters over the water! For swift messengers will go to a lofty nation and a foreign and harsh people—who is beyond it?—a hopeless and trampled nation. Now the land’s rivers,

Isaiah 18:3.text: all are like an inhabited country; their country will be inhabited as when a signal is raised from a mountain, and it will be audible like a trumpet’s voice.

Isaiah 18:4.text: For thus the Lord said to me, “There will be security in My city, like the light of midday heat, and it will be like a dew cloud on a harvest day.”

Isaiah 18:5.text: Before harvest, when the bloom is complete and the unripe grape blossoms as its flower forms unripe fruit, He will remove the small grape clusters with sickles, remove the vine branches and cut them down,

Isaiah 18:6.text: and leave them together for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts. Heaven’s birds will gather upon them, and all the earth’s wild beasts will come upon him.

Isaiah 18:7.text: At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord Sabaoth from a people afflicted and plucked, and from a great people from now on and for everlasting time—a hoping and trampled nation, which is in a part of its country’s river—to the place where the Lord Sabaoth’s name was called, Mount Zion.

Isaiah 19:1.text: A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt; Egypt’s handmade objects will be shaken before Him, and their heart overcome within them.

Isaiah 19:2.text: Egyptians will be roused against Egyptians; each will fight his brother and each his neighbor, city against city and district against district.

Isaiah 19:3.text: The Egyptians’ spirit will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will inquire of their gods, their statues, those speaking from the earth and the belly-speakers.

Isaiah 19:4.text: I will hand Egypt into the hands of harsh human masters, and harsh kings will rule them. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.

Isaiah 19:5.text: The Egyptians will drink water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.

Isaiah 19:6.text: Rivers and the river’s canals will fail, and every gathering of water dry up, in every marsh of reed and papyrus,

Isaiah 19:7.text: and all the green marsh growth around the river and everything sown by the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.

Isaiah 19:8.text: Fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan; those casting seines and those using casting nets will mourn.

Isaiah 19:9.text: Shame will seize those working split flax and those working fine linen,

Isaiah 19:10.text: and those warping them will be in pain, and all who make beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.

Isaiah 19:11.text: Tanis’s rulers will be fools; the king’s wise counselors—their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are sons of the discerning, sons of kings from the beginning”?

Isaiah 19:12.text: Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.

Isaiah 19:13.text: Tanis’s rulers failed, and Memphis’s rulers were exalted; they will lead Egypt astray tribe by tribe.

Isaiah 19:14.text: For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering; they led Egypt astray in all their works, as someone wanders while drunk and vomiting.

Isaiah 19:15.text: There will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce a head and tail, a beginning and end.

Isaiah 19:16.text: On that day the Egyptians will be like women in fear and trembling before the Lord Sabaoth’s hand, which He Himself will bring upon them.

Isaiah 19:17.text: The Judeans’ country will become a terror to the Egyptians; whenever anyone names her to them, they will fear because of the counsel the Lord has counseled against her.

Isaiah 19:18.text: On that day five cities in Egypt will speak the Canaanite language and swear by the Lord’s name. One city will be called City-Asedek.

Isaiah 19:19.text: On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the Egyptians’ country and a pillar to the Lord by its border,

Isaiah 19:20.text: and it will be an everlasting sign to the Lord in Egypt’s country, because they will cry to the Lord on account of their oppressors. The Lord will send them a man who will save them; judging, he will save them.

Isaiah 19:21.text: The Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will make sacrifices, vow vows to the Lord and pay them.

Isaiah 19:22.text: The Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them with healing. They will turn back to the Lord, and He will listen to them and heal them.

Isaiah 19:23.text: On that day there will be a road from Egypt toward the Assyrians. Assyrians will enter Egypt, and Egyptians go toward the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.

Isaiah 19:24.text: On that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and Egyptians, blessed upon the earth,

Isaiah 19:25.text: which the Lord Sabaoth blessed, saying, “Blessed be My people in Egypt and among the Assyrians, and My inheritance Israel.”

Isaiah 20:1.text: In the year Tanathan entered Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and fought Azotus and seized it,

Isaiah 20:2.text: then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and untie the sandals on your feet.” He did so, going naked and without sandals.

Isaiah 20:3.text: The Lord said, “As Isaiah My servant has gone naked and without sandals for three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;

Isaiah 20:4.text: for thus the king of the Assyrians will lead Egypt’s and the Ethiopians’ captivity, young men and elders, naked and without sandals, exposed as Egypt’s shame.

Isaiah 20:5.text: The Egyptians will be ashamed in defeat because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had trusted, for they were their glory.

Isaiah 20:6.text: Those dwelling on this island will say, ‘Behold, we had trusted that we could flee to them for help, but they could not be saved from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, shall we be saved?’”

Isaiah 21:1.text: The vision of the wilderness. As a squall might pass through a wilderness, coming from a wilderness, from a land—a fearsome

Isaiah 21:2.text: and harsh vision was announced to me. The faithless person deals faithlessly, and the lawless person acts lawlessly. The Elamites are against me, and Persian envoys come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.

Isaiah 21:3.text: Therefore my loins filled with weakness, and labor pains seized me like a woman giving birth. I did wrong by not hearing; I strove not to see.

Isaiah 21:4.text: My heart wanders, and lawlessness submerges me; my soul stands in fear.

Isaiah 21:5.text: Prepare the table; drink, eat! Rise, rulers; prepare shields!

Isaiah 21:6.text: For thus the Lord said to me: “Go, station a watcher for yourself, and report whatever you see.

Isaiah 21:7.text: I saw mounted riders, two horsemen, a donkey rider and a camel rider. Listen with great attention,

Isaiah 21:8.text: and call Uriah to the Lord’s watchtower.” He said, “I stood continually by day, and at the camp I stood all night,

Isaiah 21:9.text: and behold, he himself comes, a rider of a two-horse team.” He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen, and all her statues and handmade objects were shattered to the ground.”

Isaiah 21:10.text: Hear, you who remain and suffer; hear what I heard from the Lord Sabaoth. Israel’s God announced it to us.

Isaiah 21:11.text: The vision of Idumea. One calls to me from Seir: “Guard the battlements.”

Isaiah 21:12.text: “I watch morning and night. If you seek, seek, and dwell beside me;

Isaiah 21:13.text: in the wood you will sleep at evening, on Daidan’s road.”

Isaiah 21:14.text: Bring water to meet the thirsty, you dwelling in Thaiman’s country; meet the fugitives with loaves,

Isaiah 21:15.text: because of the multitude of those fleeing, the multitude of those wandering, the multitude of the sword, the multitude of ready arrows, and the multitude of those fallen in war.

Isaiah 21:16.text: For thus the Lord said to me: “Yet one year, like a hired worker’s year, and the glory of Kedar’s sons will fail,

Isaiah 21:17.text: and the remaining arrows of Kedar’s strong sons will be few, because the Lord, Israel’s God, has spoken.”

Isaiah 22:1.text: The utterance of Zion’s ravine. What happened to you now, that you all went up to the roofs,

Isaiah 22:2.text: the futile roofs? The city was filled with people crying out. Your wounded were not wounded by a sword, nor did your dead die in war.

Isaiah 22:3.text: All your rulers have fled; those captured are harshly bound, and the strong among you have fled far away.

Isaiah 22:4.text: Therefore I said, “Leave me; I will weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting me over the shattering of the daughter of my race.”

Isaiah 22:5.text: For there is a day of disturbance, destruction, trampling and wandering from the Lord Sabaoth in Zion’s ravine. They wander from small to great; they wander upon the mountains.

Isaiah 22:6.text: The Elamites took quivers—mounted men upon horses and an assembled battle line.

Isaiah 22:7.text: Your chosen ravines will be filled with chariots, and the horsemen will block your gates,

Isaiah 22:8.text: and they will uncover Judah’s gates and look on that day into the city’s choice houses,

Isaiah 22:9.text: and uncover the hidden things of the houses in David’s citadel. They saw that they were many and that the old pool’s water had been diverted into the city,

Isaiah 22:10.text: and that Jerusalem’s houses had been pulled down to fortify the city’s wall.

Isaiah 22:11.text: You provided water for yourselves between the two walls, inside the old pool, and did not look to the One who made her from the beginning or see the One who founded her.

Isaiah 22:12.text: The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,

Isaiah 22:13.text: but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”

Isaiah 22:14.text: These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”

Isaiah 22:15.text: Thus says the Lord Sabaoth: “Go into the chamber to Somnas the treasurer, and say to him,

Isaiah 22:16.text: What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you quarried yourself a memorial here, made yourself a memorial on high and inscribed yourself a dwelling in rock?

Isaiah 22:17.text: Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will cast out and crush a man and remove your robe,

Isaiah 22:18.text: and your glorious crown, and throw you into a great and immeasurable country. There you will die; He will make your fine chariot dishonored and your ruler’s house a trampling place,

Isaiah 22:19.text: and you will be removed from your stewardship and your standing.

Isaiah 22:20.text: On that day I will call My servant Eliakim, son of Chelkias,

Isaiah 22:21.text: clothe him in your robe, give him your crown, and put the power and your stewardship in his hands. He will be like a father to those dwelling in Jerusalem and those dwelling in Judah.

Isaiah 22:22.text: I will give him David’s glory, and he will rule, with no one contradicting.

Isaiah 22:23.text: I will establish him as a ruler in a trustworthy place, and he will become a throne of glory for his father’s house.

Isaiah 22:24.text: Every glorious person in his father’s house, from small to great, will trust in him, and they will hang upon him.

Isaiah 22:25.text: On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the person established in a trustworthy place will be shaken and fall, and the glory upon him will be removed, because the Lord has spoken.”

Isaiah 23:1.text: The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she has perished, and they no longer come from the Kitians’ land; she has been led captive.

Isaiah 23:2.text: Whom have the island-dwelling traders of Phoenicia become like, crossing the sea

Isaiah 23:3.text: upon much water, seed of traders? Like a harvest being brought in are the nations’ traders.

Isaiah 23:4.text: “Be ashamed, Sidon,” said the sea; and the sea’s strength said, “I did not labor or give birth or rear young men or raise maidens.”

Isaiah 23:5.text: When it becomes known to Egypt, pain will seize them concerning Tyre.

Isaiah 23:6.text: Go away to Carthage! Wail, residents of this island!

Isaiah 23:7.text: Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was handed over?

Isaiah 23:8.text: Who planned these things against Tyre? Is she weaker, or has she no strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.

Isaiah 23:9.text: The Lord Sabaoth planned it, to dissolve all the insolence of the glorious and dishonor everything glorious upon the earth.

Isaiah 23:10.text: Work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.

Isaiah 23:11.text: Your hand no longer has strength at sea, the hand that provoked kings. The Lord Sabaoth commanded concerning Canaan, to destroy her strength.

Isaiah 23:12.text: They will say, “You shall no longer continue in insolence and in wronging Sidon’s daughter.” Even if you go to the Kitians, there too you will have no rest,

Isaiah 23:13.text: and into the Chaldeans’ land: this too has been devastated by the Assyrians. There too you will have no rest, because her wall has fallen.

Isaiah 23:14.text: Wail, ships of Carthage, because your fortress has perished!

Isaiah 23:15.text: On that day Tyre will be left for seventy years, like a king’s time, like a person’s time. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a prostitute’s song:

Isaiah 23:16.text: “Take a lyre, wander through cities, forgotten prostitute! Play the lyre well, sing much, so that you may be remembered.”

Isaiah 23:17.text: After seventy years God will visit Tyre, and she will again be restored to her former state and become a trading center for all the inhabited world’s kingdoms.

Isaiah 23:18.text: Her trade and her wage will be holy to the Lord. It will not be collected for them; instead, all her trade will be for those dwelling before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, as a contribution, a memorial before the Lord.

Isaiah 24:1.text: Behold, the Lord is destroying the inhabited world; He will make it desolate, uncover its face and scatter those dwelling in it.

Isaiah 24:2.text: The people will be like the priest, the slave like the master, the maidservant like the mistress; the buyer will be like the seller, the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one to whom he owes a debt.

Isaiah 24:3.text: The earth will be utterly destroyed, and the earth utterly plundered, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken these things.

Isaiah 24:4.text: The earth mourned, the inhabited world was destroyed, and the earth’s high ones mourned.

Isaiah 24:5.text: The earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in it, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.

Isaiah 24:6.text: Therefore a curse will consume the earth, because those dwelling in it sinned. Therefore those dwelling on the earth will be poor, and few people will be left.

Isaiah 24:7.text: Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.

Isaiah 24:8.text: The joy of tambourines has ceased; the impudence and wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the lyre’s sound has ceased.

Isaiah 24:9.text: They were ashamed and did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking it.

Isaiah 24:10.text: Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.

Isaiah 24:11.text: Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.

Isaiah 24:12.text: Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.

Isaiah 24:13.text: All these things will happen on the earth, among the nations: as when someone gleans an olive tree, so they will glean them, even when the grape harvest has ceased.

Isaiah 24:14.text: These will cry aloud, and those left upon the earth will rejoice together with the Lord’s glory. The sea’s water will be troubled;

Isaiah 24:15.text: therefore the Lord’s glory will be in the sea’s islands; the Lord’s name will be glorious—O Lord, Israel’s God!

Isaiah 24:16.text: From the earth’s wings we heard wonders: “Hope for the devout!” And they will say, “Woe to those who reject, those who reject the law!”

Isaiah 24:17.text: Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!

Isaiah 24:18.text: Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.

Isaiah 24:19.text: The earth will be utterly agitated, and the earth will be utterly at a loss;

Isaiah 24:20.text: The earth has tilted and will be shaken like a fruit-watcher’s shelter, like someone drunk and hungover. It will fall and will never be able to rise, for lawlessness has prevailed upon it.

Isaiah 24:21.text: God will bring His hand against heaven’s array and against the earth’s kings.

Isaiah 24:22.text: They will gather and shut them into a fortress and a prison; after many generations there will be a visitation of them.

Isaiah 24:23.text: The brick will melt and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem and will be glorified before the elders.

Isaiah 25:1.text: Lord my God, I will glorify Thee and sing Thy name, because Thou hast done wondrous things, an ancient, true plan. May it be so, Lord!

Isaiah 25:2.text: For Thou hast made cities a mound, fortified cities so that their foundations fall. The city of the ungodly will certainly never be rebuilt.

Isaiah 25:3.text: Therefore the poor people will bless Thee, and cities of wronged people will bless Thee.

Isaiah 25:4.text: For Thou didst become a helper to every lowly city and a shelter to those discouraged by need. Thou wilt rescue them from evil people, a shelter for the thirsty and a breath for wronged people.

Isaiah 25:5.text: They will bless Thee like fainthearted people thirsting in Zion because of ungodly people, to whom Thou didst hand us over.

Isaiah 25:6.text: The Lord Sabaoth will act for all the nations upon this mountain. They will drink gladness, drink wine and anoint themselves with perfume.

Isaiah 25:7.text: On this mountain, hand all these things over to the nations, for this plan concerns all the nations.

Isaiah 25:8.text: Death swallowed, having prevailed; and again God removed every tear from every face. He removed the people’s reproach from all the earth, for the Lord’s mouth has spoken.

Isaiah 25:9.text: On that day they will say, “Behold, our God, in whom we hoped and exulted; and we will rejoice in our salvation.”

Isaiah 25:10.text: For God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moab’s land will be trampled as people tread a threshing floor with wagons,

Isaiah 25:11.text: and he will release his hands, just as he himself brought low for destruction; he will bring low his insolence over what he laid his hands on,

Isaiah 25:12.text: and he will bring low the height of your wall’s refuge, and it will descend to the ground.

Isaiah 26:1.text: On that day they will sing this song in Judah’s land, saying, “Behold, a fortified city! He will make our salvation a wall and an encircling wall.

Isaiah 26:2.text: Open the gates; let a people enter, keeping righteousness and keeping truth,

Isaiah 26:3.text: holding fast to truth and keeping peace. For in Thee

Isaiah 26:4.text: they hoped, Lord, for ever, the great, everlasting God,

Isaiah 26:5.text: Thou who didst humble and bring down those dwelling on high. Thou wilt cast down fortified cities and bring them to the ground,

Isaiah 26:6.text: and the feet of the meek and lowly will trample them.

Isaiah 26:7.text: The way of the devout became straight, and the way of the devout is prepared.

Isaiah 26:8.text: For the Lord’s way is judgment. We hoped in Thy name and in the remembrance

Isaiah 26:9.text: which our soul desires. From night my spirit rises early toward Thee, God, because Thine ordinances are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, you dwelling upon the earth!

Isaiah 26:10.text: For the ungodly has ceased; he will certainly not learn righteousness upon the earth or practice truth. Let the ungodly be removed, so that he may not see the Lord’s glory.

Isaiah 26:11.text: Lord, Thine arm is high, and they did not know; when they know, they will be ashamed. Zeal will seize an undisciplined people, and now fire will consume the opponents.

Isaiah 26:12.text: Lord our God, give us peace, for Thou hast repaid everything to us.

Isaiah 26:13.text: Lord our God, acquire us! Lord, we know no other besides Thee; we name Thy name.

Isaiah 26:14.text: The dead will certainly not see life, nor will physicians ever raise them. Therefore Thou didst bring calamity, destroy and remove every male of theirs.

Isaiah 26:15.text: Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to all the earth’s glorious people!

Isaiah 26:16.text: Lord, in affliction I remembered Thee; in slight affliction Thy discipline was for us.

Isaiah 26:17.text: Like a woman in labor nearing childbirth and crying out in her pang, so we became toward Thy beloved because of fear of Thee, Lord.

Isaiah 26:18.text: We conceived, labored and gave birth; we produced the spirit of Thy salvation upon the earth, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.

Isaiah 26:19.text: The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”

Isaiah 26:20.text: Go, My people, enter your inner rooms, shut your door, hide for a little, a very little while, until the Lord’s wrath passes.

Isaiah 26:21.text: For behold, the Lord brings wrath from the holy place upon those dwelling on the earth. The earth will uncover its blood and will not cover those killed.

Isaiah 27:1.text: On that day God will bring the holy, great and strong sword against the dragon, the fleeing serpent, against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and will kill the dragon.

Isaiah 27:2.text: On that day, a beautiful vineyard; a desire to lead a song against her.

Isaiah 27:3.text: “I am a strong city, a besieged city; in vain I will water her, for she will be captured by night, and by day the wall will fall.

Isaiah 27:4.text: There is none who has not seized her. Who will set me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I rejected her.” Therefore, for this reason the Lord God has done everything He commanded. “I have been burned!”

Isaiah 27:5.text: the residents in her will cry. “Let us make peace with Him; let us make peace.”

Isaiah 27:6.text: Those coming, Jacob’s children—Israel will sprout and flower, and the inhabited world will be filled with his fruit.

Isaiah 27:7.text: Surely he will not be struck just as he himself struck, and be killed just as he himself killed?

Isaiah 27:8.text: Fighting and reproaching, he will send them away. Wast Thou not the One planning with a harsh spirit to destroy them with a spirit of wrath?

Isaiah 27:9.text: Therefore Jacob’s lawlessness will be removed, and this is his blessing: when I remove his sin, when they make all altar stones cut down like fine dust. Their trees will certainly not remain, and their idols will be cut down like a forest far away.

Isaiah 27:10.text: The inhabited flock will be released like an abandoned flock; it will be pasture for a long time, and there they will rest.

Isaiah 27:11.text: After a time there will be nothing green in her because it has dried. Women coming from a spectacle, come! For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will certainly not pity them, nor will the One who formed them ever have mercy.

Isaiah 27:12.text: On that day the Lord will fence off from the River’s canal to Rhinocorura; but you, gather Israel’s sons one by one.

Isaiah 27:13.text: On that day they will sound the great trumpet. Those lost in the Assyrians’ country and those lost in Egypt will come and bow to the Lord upon the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

2 Kings 16:7.text: Ahaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, ‘I am your slave and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising against me.’

2 Kings 16:8.text: Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the Lord’s house and the king’s house, and sent gifts to the king.

2 Kings 16:9.text: The king of the Assyrians listened to him. The king of the Assyrians went up against Damascus, captured it, deported it, and put Raasson to death.

2 Kings 16:10.text: King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians. He saw the altar in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest the altar’s likeness and design for all its construction.

2 Kings 16:11.text: Uriah the priest built the altar in accordance with everything King Ahaz sent from Damascus.

2 Kings 17:3.text: Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.

2 Kings 17:4.text: The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.

2 Kings 17:5.text: The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

2 Kings 17:6.text: In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.

2 Kings 17:7.text: This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.

2 Kings 17:8.text: They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,

Zephaniah 2:11.text: The Lord will appear against them and destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth. All the islands of the nations will worship Him, each from his place.

Zephaniah 2:12.text: You too, Ethiopians, are slain by My sword.
